title: If math is more than proof, we need to better celebrate the rest of it
summary: Fields Medalist Terry Tao argues that mathematics is too narrowly defined as just proof-writing, while other essential aspects like intuition, heuristics, examples, failed attempts, and analogy-building are undervalued and undercelebrated in the mathematical community.
problem_solved: Addresses the imbalance in how mathematical contributions are valued, with proofs dominating while the creative and exploratory work of mathematics is overlooked.
why_valuable: It provides a nuanced perspective from a top mathematician on how to better recognize and nurture the full spectrum of mathematical thinking, which could improve mathematical education and research culture.
